sections.content:
The player is still at rows 37-39, and the G frame at 32-35 was converted to white. The player did NOT move up after SPACE. So the mechanic is:
- UP creates a G frame in the direction of movement (above the player)
- SPACE converts the G frame to white
- The player does NOT move automatically
This means the player is stationary and the UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT actions place G frames in those directions, which can then be converted to white with SPACE. The goal is likely to convert all the charcoal frames to white by building a path of white frames toward them.
Wait, but earlier the player DID move from rows 41-43 to 37-39. Let me reconsider...
Actually, looking back at the history:
- Initial position: player at rows 41-43 (green block)
- After first UP: player at rows 37-39
- After second UP: player stayed at 37-39, but a G frame appeared at 32-35
So the first UP moved the player, but subsequent UPs just create G frames. Why did the first UP move the player? Maybe the first UP moved the player because there was no frame above them. When there's a frame (or the space is occupied), UP creates a new G frame instead of moving.
Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the mechanic is:
- The player can only move into white space
- UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT creates a G frame in the direction of movement if the space is not white
- SPACE converts the adjacent G frame to white
- The player then moves into the white space
So the sequence would be:
1. UP creates G frame above
2. SPACE converts G to white
3. Player moves into white space (automatically or with another UP)
But the player didn't move after the last SPACE. Maybe the player only moves when they press UP again, and there's white space above.
Let me try UP again to see if the player moves into the white space.
